title: GDScript exported properties
key_points: Class members can be exported in Godot, meaning their value gets saved along with the resource they're attached to.
Exported properties are visible and editable in the editor, allowing artists and game designers to modify values that influence how the program runs.
The @export annotation is used to export member variables.
Exporting properties can also be done in other languages such as C#, with syntax varying depending on the language.
Resources and nodes can be exported as properties in a script without having to use NodePaths.
limitations: Exported arrays must have initializers that are constant expressions.
Using @export variables for Resource objects makes them a dependency of the instance, meaning all referenced resources are loaded when the containing scene is loaded.
If you want to reference a Resource object but load it manually when you need it, use @export_file or @export_file_path instead.
asserts: Class members can be exported in Godot, allowing their values to be saved and edited along with the resource they're attached to.
scope: The assertion applies to class members being exported within a script, enabling their values to be saved and edited alongside the associated resource.
